newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA WEIGHS CARLSBERG, BBH OFFERS FOR BREWER.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA WEIGHS CARLSBERG, BBH OFFERS FOR BREWER.

text.p: Lithuania said on Tuesday it will submit investment offers by Danish Carlsberg and Hartwall /Orkla venture Baltic Beverage Holdings (BBH) to shareholders of state-run Utena Beverages.

"The agricultural ministry aims to present the competing offers of Carlsberg and BBH to the shareholders' meeting of Utena," European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene, who has been handling privatisation matters, told a news conference.
She also said that during a recent trip to Copenhagen she met Carlsberg reprsentatives.
The Utena shareholder meeting is scheduled for July 27.
Baltic Beverage is already very active in the Baltics, owning majorities in Lithuania's second largest brewer Kalnapilis, Latvia's biggest beer maker Aldaris and Estonian market leader Saku.
Utena Beverages has said it has a letter of intent with a potential investor but would not name the company.
Carlsberg said it has had contacts with the Lithuanian firm but has not revealed any details.
Utena says it needs investment of 60 million litas to 80 million litas to modernise its output.
The company has also been involved in a long-running legal dispute with the government over how big a stake the state owns in the company.
It has made several unsuccessful attempts to register its shares with the securities commission, a first step to entering the stock market and being privatised.
Utena says the state owns 21.5 percent of the company but the government sees its stake as more than 40 percent.
"The government must solve the dispute over the ownership of shares," Andrikiene said.
